notes: Seeded semantic test defects that the testing lane missed in production on 2026-08-19.
Each defect is self-contained: everything needed to resolve it is inside the supplied diff,
so a miss is a reasoning/attention failure, not a missing-evidence failure.
Clean fixtures are controls: a charter change that raises detection by making the lane
indiscriminate is not an improvement, so false positives are measured in the same run.
2026-08-19 corpus-expansion note: the original three defect fixtures above all target the
charter's newest 'deep' additions (vacuous default-value assertions, formatting-evadable
guards). None exercised the charter's original base Flag list -- exclusive/skipped markers
left active, or shared mutable state / execution-order dependence between tests -- which had
zero regression coverage in this matrix despite being two of the charter's four founding
that gap; each is paired with a near-miss clean control (table-driven-consolidation-
preserves-coverage, function-scoped-fixture-avoids-shared-state) shaped to trip a reviewer
that pattern-matches on surface signals ('fewer it() blocks', 'a module-level let') rather
2026-08-25 holdout expansion: paired Elixir branch-coverage and Java asynchronous-wait
fixtures exercise the same causal review principles in different languages and test
frameworks. Their identifiers and grading vocabulary are evaluation-only and are never
included in the testing persona's runtime instructions.

fixtures.title: Guard against checking out the pull request base SHA
fixtures.summary: A security guard written as `not in` over a 4-line literal block, so reordering or reindenting the workflow options silently disables it.

files.patch:
@@ -8,10 +8,11 @@ jobs:
   review:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v5
         with:
           persist-credentials: false
+          fetch-depth: 0
       - run: node ./bin/review.mjs

@@ -1,6 +1,20 @@
 from pathlib import Path
 
 WORKFLOW = Path(".github/workflows/pr-review.yml").read_text()
 
+# Checking out the pull request base SHA would run untrusted head content with
+# base credentials. This must never appear in the review workflow.
+FORBIDDEN_CHECKOUT = """      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+"""
+
+
+def test_workflow_never_checks_out_base_sha():
+    assert FORBIDDEN_CHECKOUT not in WORKFLOW

fixtures.title: Anchor the base-SHA guard on the semantic token
fixtures.summary: Control: the guard parses the workflow, anchors on every semantic form of a base ref, and asserts it inspected at least one checkout step so it cannot pass vacuously. Nothing to flag.

files.patch:
@@ -1,10 +1,30 @@
 import yaml
 from pathlib import Path
 
 WORKFLOW = yaml.safe_load(Path(".github/workflows/pr-review.yml").read_text())
 
+# Every expression GitHub offers for the base side of a pull request. A checkout that resolves
+# any of them runs untrusted head content against base credentials.
+BASE_REF_TOKENS = ("base.sha", "base.ref", "base_ref", "base_sha")
+
+
+def checkout_steps():
+    for job in WORKFLOW["jobs"].values():
+        for step in job.get("steps", []):
+            if str(step.get("uses", "")).startswith("actions/checkout"):
+                yield step
+
+
+def test_no_checkout_step_resolves_a_base_ref():
+    inspected = 0
+    for step in checkout_steps():
+        inspected += 1
+        ref = str(step.get("with", {}).get("ref", ""))
+        for token in BASE_REF_TOKENS:
+            assert token not in ref, f"checkout step resolves a base ref via {token}: {ref}"
+    # Without this the loop passes on a workflow that checks out nothing at all.
+    assert inspected > 0, "no checkout step was inspected; the guard would pass vacuously"

fixtures.title: Consolidate the marker-routing cases into a table-driven test
fixtures.summary: Control: two separate it() blocks become one it.each() over the same two cases. Assertion count and coverage are identical; a reviewer that pattern-matches on 'fewer it() blocks' as a proxy for 'fewer tests' would false-positive here.

fixtures.title: Add rate-limiter coverage with a fresh instance per test
fixtures.summary: Control: same three cases as the paired defect fixture, but the limiter is constructed in beforeEach and the third test drives its own two setup calls instead of relying on the first two tests having already run. Order-independent by construction; nothing to flag.

fixtures.title: Return distinct errors for absent and blank webhook targets
fixtures.summary: The changed function introduces separate absent-target and blank-target branches, but the new tests exercise only the absent case, leaving the blank branch and its distinct diagnostic unproved.

files.patch:
@@ -1,7 +1,11 @@
 defmodule WebhookTargetTest do
   use ExUnit.Case, async: true
 
+  test "rejects a missing target" do
+    assert WebhookTarget.resolve(nil) == {:error, :missing_target}
+  end
+
   test "normalizes a configured target" do
     assert WebhookTarget.resolve(%{target: "  ops  "}) == {:ok, "ops"}
   end
 end

fixtures.title: Cover both invalid webhook target forms
fixtures.summary: Control: the changed function introduces two distinct invalid-input branches and the table-driven test exercises both causes and their separate diagnostics.

files.patch:
@@ -1,7 +1,16 @@
 defmodule WebhookTargetTest do
   use ExUnit.Case, async: true
 
+  for {input, reason} <- [
+        {nil, :missing_target},
+        {%{target: ""}, :blank_target}
+      ] do
+    test "rejects invalid target as #{reason}" do
+      assert WebhookTarget.resolve(unquote(Macro.escape(input))) ==
+               {:error, unquote(reason)}
+    end
+  end
+
   test "normalizes a configured target" do
     assert WebhookTarget.resolve(%{target: "  ops  "}) == {:ok, "ops"}
   end
 end
